findings.title: Goroutine leak on panic in executeStructured
findings.body: The startStructuredOutputCapture function starts a goroutine that runs indefinitely until cancelled. In executeStructured (line 114), the cleanup function is called immediately after app.Harness returns, but there is no defer statement. If app.Harness panics, the cleanup function is never called, causing the goroutine to leak indefinitely. The goroutine will continue looping, calling filepath.Glob every 20ms and consuming CPU resources.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: executeStructured calls startStructuredOutputCapture at line 114, which starts a goroutine that loops until cancelled
Step 2: The goroutine executes `for { scan(); select { case <-watchCtx.Done(): return; case <-ticker.C: } }` indefinitely
Step 3: If app.Harness(ctx, prompt, schema, &dest, opts) at line 115 panics, the function stack unwinds
Step 4: The cleanup function stopOutputCapture() at line 116 is never called due to the panic
Step 5: The goroutine continues running indefinitely, calling filepath.Glob every 20ms without cleanup
findings.suggestion: Modify executeStructured to use a defer statement to ensure cleanup is called even if app.Harness panics. Change the pattern from: `stopOutputCapture := startStructuredOutputCapture[T](ctx, opts.ProjectDir, schema); result, err := app.Harness(...); capturedOutput := stopOutputCapture()` to: `var capturedOutput []byte; stopOutputCapture := startStructuredOutputCapture[T](ctx, opts.ProjectDir, schema); defer func() { capturedOutput = stopOutputCapture() }(); result, err := app.Harness(...)`
